disposition_reason: The registered task estimates biological changes after rewarded or unrewarded visual experience. More selective cells, larger learning contrasts, or smaller p-values are not better predictions by a candidate method. Altering the analysis to maximize these observations would change the scientific estimand; a new animal-held-out decoder would be a separately registered extension.

source_paper.title: Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks

evidence.locator: Results: Supervised and unsupervised plasticity; Figures 1, 4 and 5; Methods: Animals
evidence.supports: Original outcomes are neural-selectivity, reward-activity and behavioral learning contrasts across experience conditions; the experimental units include longitudinally observed mice.
Author code computes descriptive response indices and fractions from complete recorded cell populations; the behavioral function uses the first 200 trials and the reward-zone lick response.

evidence.locator: Version 2 description and files manifest; DOI 10.25378/janelia.28811129.v2
evidence.supports: Release supplies neural, behavioral, retinotopy and dimensionality-reduction files, including the three behavior-only pretraining cohorts. Metadata was reviewed; no array payload was read.

target.description: Estimate experience-associated changes in selectivity, representations and subsequent licking behavior, preserving the original rewarded, unrewarded and control conditions.

dataset.description: Janelia Figshare article 28811129 version 2, DOI 10.25378/janelia.28811129.v2; all relevant original recording/behavior sessions rather than a selected cell subset.

cohort.description: Original longitudinal imaging mice and separate behavior-only cohorts; source Figure 5 contains natural-image pretraining, grating pretraining and no-pretraining groups. Session histories must remain attached to each animal.

split.description: These registered biological contrasts do not define a candidate training/validation/test partition. Original coding-direction analysis splits do not turn the main descriptive findings into a generalization benchmark.

inputs.description: Calcium-derived spks with stimulus and running/corridor alignment, retinotopy area identities, and behavioral lick/reward records.

preprocessing.description: Preserve author running/texture-frame selection, all-cell area denominators, stimulus IDs and source interpolation; author dprime uses population standard deviations with NaN-aware reductions.

metric.description: Descriptive dprime is 2*(mean1-mean2)/(sd1+sd2); area fractions count cells passing each threshold. Reward-zone lick probabilities and their rewarded-minus-unrewarded contrast describe animals, not candidate prediction error.

aggregation.description: Author fraction arrays retain visual-area, mouse/session and threshold axes; behavior-only outputs retain mouse and day. Repeated cells/trials are not independent animals.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered candidate-performance endpoint for the registered biological contrasts

published_baseline.description: Published neural and behavioral effects are observations to estimate, not a performance score to exceed.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Replaying author indices would calibrate a reconstruction; it would not establish a competitive method baseline.

minimum_effect.rationale: Increasing an observed biological contrast is not an improvement objective.

uncertainty.method: No candidate-win uncertainty rule applies. Original mouse-level descriptive inference is retained for calibration.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Mouse, retaining repeated sessions and exposure history
uncertainty.rationale: Cells, frames and repeated trials cannot supply independent biological replications or convert an effect estimate into method performance.

paper_win_requires: No same-task paper win is admitted for this registration as currently defined.
Do not count higher dprime, more selective neurons, a larger licking contrast, or stronger significance as improvement.
A predictive method or different training intervention needs a separately reviewed task with its own source-paper comparator; an animal-held-out extension is not this paper's original comparison.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is defined for these descriptive outcomes.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive: retain descriptive reconstruction and source-method auditing only.
episode.candidate_freeze: No candidate improvement program is admitted for this endpoint.
episode.final_evaluation: Historical selectivity/reward/lick computations are calibration outputs only.
episode.baseline_policy: Author formulas remain reconstruction references; locally authored matched-cohort or held-animal analyses do not become paper baselines.

blocking_issues: No defensible direction of better candidate performance exists for the registered descriptive estimands.
Existing evaluator lacks complete coding-direction and spatial-density analysis and has unresolved sequence threshold/trial-split semantics; these remain reproduction issues.
Any replacement must establish a source-backed ordered task without relabeling this biological contrast or silently narrowing the original population.

legacy.notes: Preserve initial-evaluator-v1 and sequence/materials as source-derived calibration. Its engineered controls, endpoint calculations and prospective equal-animal summaries are not stronger-than-paper evidence.
